subject: MSA + Order Form: allocation of defense & evidence access for third-party IP claims (Nebula Systems)

Cc: procurement@nebulasys.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form — third-party IP claims (initial ask)

Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Nebula ran the MSA + Order Form redlines by legal and outside counsel overnight and the primary outstanding commercial/legal item is indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from model output or components of the service.

High-level asks from our side:
- Vendor (Redwood) must defend and indemnify Nebula for third-party IP infringement claims tied to the service outputs, including claims based on model weights or shipped components.
- Nebula requires the right to hand back control only in narrow circumstances (conflict of interest).
- We need a clear evidence access SLA so Nebula can obtain logs and training-hash artifacts for litigation triage (7-day turnaround).
- Nebula wants a payment of legal fees and costs up front if the vendor requests control.

Attached are our redlines (PDF) and a short mark-up from our counsel. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these asks or propose a narrowed alternative this week — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Cheers,
Laura Hill
Head of Procurement, Nebula Systems
laura.hill@nebulasys.com

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Laura Hill <laura.hill@nebulasys.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — third-party IP claims (initial ask)

Laura — thanks for the redlines and the clear list of asks. We appreciate the urgency. High-level response from Redwood:

1) Defense control: Redwood is willing to take primary defense for third-party infringement claims that result solely from Redwood-delivered model artifacts (base model weights, infra code we ship). We can accept control in that narrow scope.

2) Customer outputs / training data: For outputs that depend on customer-supplied data (fine-tuning or uploaded content), we propose Nebula retain the right to conduct the initial defense or at least co-control if the customer's data materially contributes to the claim. This protects both parties and aligns incentives.

3) Evidence access SLA: Redwood can commit to 10 business days for logs/exports in non-litigation triage. For active litigation, we'll commit to expedited production but ask Nebula to route requests through our legal team to avoid scope creep.

4) Legal fees and costs: We cannot accept a blanket upfront fee payment for invoking control. We propose a shared-cost mechanism: Redwood covers reasonable defense costs when we take control; if Nebula takes control for claims tied to customer content, Nebula covers costs. We can add an insurance-offset and a cap on combined defense costs tied to the Order Form value (example: 2x annual spend), subject to negotiation.

Attached: RWND_MSA_redlines_draft_v3.docx (legal suggested language). Kimberley and Marissa on legal are looped for specific clause text. Ben/Jordan from commercial for pricing/contract mechanics.

Next steps: Laura, can your counsel indicate if the shared-cost + control-by-scope approach is acceptable? If so, we can route a redline with specific clause language today.

Best —
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Hill <laura.hill@nebulasys.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — third-party IP claims (initial ask)

Soojin,

Thanks for the quick reply and for proposing a split by scope. Our outside counsel is concerned about two items:

- Nebula needs the right to retain exclusive defense control even when Redwood claims the infringement is solely on the vendor side, if Nebula reasonably believes Redwood's defense creates an irreconcilable conflict or compromises Nebula's remedies.
- The proposed cost-sharing cap tied to spend is workable only if there is a carve-out for injunctive relief or statutory damages — we want those to remain uncapped.

Our counsel attached a short memo and highlighted sections in the PDF. If Redwood wants to preserve the cap approach, can Redwood accept an explicit carve-out for equitable relief and for third-party claims where statutory penalties are likely?

We are aiming to finalize the Order Form this week. If you can provide final clause text and a response to counsel's memo by EOD today Pacific, procurement will expedite approval.

—Laura

Attachments: Nebula_counsel_memo_070721.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Jul 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed compromise language and evidence owner matrix

Team — drafting note and negotiation posture. Summary of recommended compromise to send to Nebula:

1) Defense control by scope: Redwood will accept defense/control for third-party claims that "aris[e] out of Redwood-provided model weights, inference runtime, or other Redwood-delivered components". Nebula can take control if Redwood's defense creates a conflict — but Nebula must provide reasonable grounds (good faith standard) and pay for reasonable incremental costs if Nebula assumes control for claims where Redwood was primary contributor.

2) Cost allocation: Shared-cost approach with a combined cap at 2x Nebula's annual committed spend (Order Form). Carve-out: statutory damages and injunctive relief are not subject to cap. We limit Redwood's indemnity for customer-input-triggered claims to reimbursement (not defense) unless Redwood materially modified the customer's inputs.

3) Evidence & logs: Redwood commits to a 7 business day turnaround for a preliminary evidence export for triage; for full production in active litigation, we will make logs, prefix cache snapshots and relevant model metadata available within 10 business days after formal request routed through legal with an agreed confidentiality/privilege protocol. We attach an evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx that maps which team will pull what artifacts.

4) Insurance/offset: If Redwood's defense triggers an insurance offset or subrogation, we will cooperate but include a mutual process for notice and waiver of subrogation where appropriate.

Attached is a redline (RWND_MSA_redlines_draft_v3.docx) with clause text. My ask: Ben/Jordan, confirm commercially whether the 2x spend cap is acceptable; Marissa, please sign off on the good-faith/assumption-of-control language.

-Kimberly
General Counsel (Corporate) — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Laura / Daniel — following internal review, Redwood is prepared to present the compromise below and route a DocuSign-ready Order Form if Nebula can agree:

- Control by scope: Redwood will accept primary defense where the claim arises from Redwood-delivered model artifacts or runtime. Nebula may assume control if there is a good-faith conflict; if Nebula assumes control for claims properly in Redwood's scope, Nebula will bear reasonable incremental costs beyond what Redwood would have paid.
- Cost cap: Combined defense cost cap = 2x Nebula's committed annual spend (example in Order Form). Carve-out: statutory damages and injunctive relief are excluded from the cap.
- Evidence access: Redwood commits to a 7 business day turnaround for triage exports and 10 business days for full production in active litigation after a formal legal request; evidence access will follow the attached evidence-owner matrix and privilege protocol.
- Insurance/subrogation: mutual notice and cooperation with an option to negotiate limited waiver of subrogation for customer-specific data claims.

If Nebula accepts, I will send a DocuSign link with the Order Form and highlighted MSA redlines for signature. Please note: this compromise is time-limited — we need confirmation within 72 hours to hold pricing and the dedicated capacity commitment.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Soojin Lee

Redwood Inference
